notes: Access: www.hay.com reached directly via HTTP (see na26.json notes for the us.hay.com/DWR redirect background and robots.txt check - no block encountered). HAY is a premium Danish design brand distributed partly via full-price retailers (e.g. Design Within Reach in the US) - it may genuinely lack a Clearance/Outlet section, and this proved to be the case after real investigation. Checked: (1) full Products mega-menu on the homepage (Furniture with all sub-categories, Lighting, Accessories) - no Sale/Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance entry; (2) footer navigation (About, B2B, Career, Contact, Designers, Catalogues, Digital showroom/library, Videos, Store locator, Press, Sustainability, Country selector, Privacy, Cookie notice, Newsletter, social links) - none; (3) sitemap-content.xml (88KB, every non-product page on the site) grepped case-insensitively for sale|outlet|clearance|discount|offer|deal|promo - zero genuine hits (the only 'sale' substring match was an unrelated news article title containing '...Autumn Table...' with no clearance connection, and 'bestsell' hits covered separately in bs26.json); (4) sitemap-products.xml (1407 product URLs) grepped for the same terms plus new-arriv/new-in - zero hits, confirming no clearance-tagged product listing path exists; (5) site's own search (Playwright, JS-rendered overlay) for 'sale', 'clearance', 'outlet' - the client-rendered search widget did not resolve to a distinct results panel in the automated pass (inconclusive on its own, not treated as proof of absence by itself), but combined with the exhaustive nav+sitemap check above (both the content sitemap and the full 1407-URL product sitemap) this is sufficient real-navigation/sitemap evidence that no genuine Clearance-type PLP exists anywhere on this catalogue. No ambiguous Sale/Offers/Promotions page was found at all to even apply the Sale-vs-Clearance test to - the site simply has no such section.
